comment_box: I am writing to express my opposition to the proposed regulation published on August 4, 2025 (RIN 2900-AS31), which aims to reinstate the exclusion of abortion services and counseling from the VA medical benefits package and CHAMPVA benefits package as specified in 38 CFR Part 17. It is the worst kind of bait and switch when the federal government removes important health benefits from those who have volunteered to put their own lives on the line for our nation. This regulation reinstates a complete exclusion that exceeds reasonable policy by removing coverage even in situations where a veteran's life or health is at risk or where the pregnancy resulted from rape or incest. There should be absolutely no restrictions put on by the federal government which would stand between personal medical decisions made by a patient and doctor, especially a patient who is a U.S. Military Veteran. In the second paragraph of the SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION section, the justification stems from the assertion that abortion services are not considered “needed” medical services under section 1710 of title 38; however, the term “needed” is not defined and should be interpreted through clinical judgment that is based on current medical standards, as care may be medically warranted in many specific situations. This exclusion will disproportionately affect veterans in rural regions or in states with higher restrictive abortion regulations, many of whom depend on the VA as their sole available medical provider. For this reason, the suggested language stating that “scope of coverage shall exclude abortion services and abortion counseling” should be amended to clearly permit exceptions where the attending VA healthcare provider considers the treatment medically necessary, especially when the veteran's life, health, or well-being is at risk, or in cases of rape or incest. It is unconscionable that Veterans who have served this country with honor are being subjected to rules that are based on religious beliefs rather than medical science. The sacred pact that we have with our veterans should not be broken for any reason and I request that this rule be amended to include that abortion counseling and services be provided when the life, health or well-being of the veteran is at risk or in the case of rape of incest.
